detaileddescription.para: NDXL can be obtained from the library's GitHub repository. The C/C++ header files are located inside the include folder, and the precompiled libraries are located inside the lib folder. Copy these folders directly into the working directory of your project, which we will assume has the following structure:
In main.c, we will define a minimal working program calling ndxlInit(), which must be called before using any NDXL functionality.

We will cover here the installation and linking guides for both the static and dynamic libraries in MSVC and gcc. Whether you use the static or dynamic version depends on you:
Use the static version for faster runtime execution but a larger executable
Use the dynamic version for a smaller executable but slower runtime execution

sect1.title: Compiling with MSVC
sect1.para: In the solution explorer, right-click your project file, and click "Properties" at the very bottom. At the top of the "Properties" dialogue, ensure the "Configuration" is set to "All Configurations", and "Platform" is set to "All Platforms". On the left, click the "Linker" dropdown, then click on "Input". At the top of the page, the "Additional Dependencies" field will likely contain:
If your project uses other libraries, they will likely already be linked here too. Add NDXL.lib to the end preceeded by a semicolon:
If the field is empty, simply set it to NDXL.lib, then click onto another field so that Visual Studio processes the input.

sect2.title: Linking against the dynamic version (.dll)

Do not define the NDXL_STATIC preprocessor definition as it will attempt to import static symbols. Finally, ensure that NDXL.dll is in the same path as your executable at runtime, otherwise you will run into a "dll not found error". Either copy the file manually to your target directory, or automate the process using a build event.

sect2.title: Linking against the dynamic version (.so)
sect2.para: Ensure that libNDXL.so is discoverable by your runtime loader when you execute the program. The easiest way to do this is to copy the file into the same directory as my-project.out and run the executable from that directory.

sect1.title: References
sect1.para: For a detailed guide on linking libraries in MSVC, see the MSVC documentation.
For a detailed guide on linking libraries in gcc, see the gcc website.
